title: Tteokgalbi Grilled Beef-and-Pork Patties
shortDescription: Ground beef and pork are mixed with a pear-soy, garlic, scallion, onion, and sesame seasoning, shaped into thick oval patties, and grilled to a verified ground-meat temperature.
culturalContext: Tteokgalbi refers to seasoned minced or finely chopped meat shaped into patties, historically connected to rib meat and several Korean regional and formal dining traditions. Recipes and origin narratives vary; this accessible beef-and-pork draft requires cultural review and does not imply that rice cake is an ingredient.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Chef’s knife and separate raw-meat cutting board
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill

finely grated and squeezed nearly dry

marinadeOrSeasoning.meatWeightCovered: 900 g / 2 pounds total ground beef and pork

Stir in pear, squeezed onion, garlic, and scallions

marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Chilled nonreactive mixing bowl, followed by a parchment-lined covered sheet pan
marinadeOrSeasoning.refrigeratedMarinationTimeRange: 30 minutes after shaping at or below 40°F / 4°C
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Cook within 24 hours of mixing; do not hold seasoned ground meat beyond the package use-by date.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve 30 ml / 2 tablespoons seasoning in a clean covered bowl before mixing the remainder into ground meat if a finishing glaze is desired.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard any seasoning or liquid that contacts raw ground meat; do not brush it onto cooked patties. Use only the separately reserved clean portion, boiled before service.

All-beef patties require a separate fat and texture test.

instructions.heading: Prepare seasoning cold
instructions.action: Keep meat refrigerated. Mix soy sauce, sugar, rice syrup, pear, squeezed onion, garlic, scallions, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and pepper. Reserve 2 tablespoons in a clean bowl before raw contact if glazing.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sugar is dissolved and the mixture is moist but not watery.
instructions.safetyNote: Label and refrigerate the clean reserve; wash produce before grating and use clean tools.

instructions.heading: Mix the ground meat
instructions.action: Add cold ground beef and pork to a chilled bowl. Pour in seasoning and mix with gloved hands just until sticky and cohesive, about 90 seconds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Mixture holds together when pressed without visible dry meat pockets.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not rinse or taste raw meat; wash hands and sanitize the bowl area after mixing.

instructions.heading: Shape and chill
instructions.action: Divide into eight 155 g portions. Shape into 10 cm / 4-inch ovals about 2 cm / 3/4 inch thick, press a shallow center indentation, place on parchment, cover, and chill 30 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Patties are equal, smooth-edged, and firm enough to lift.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep raw patties below ready-to-eat foods in the refrigerator and discard raw-contact parchment after use.

instructions.heading: Preheat safely
instructions.action: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill to medium and oil lightly. Set separate raw and cooked spatulas and platters.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Grill is hot, clean, lightly oiled, and arranged with separate utensil zones.
instructions.safetyNote: Never use charcoal, propane, or other fuel-burning grills indoors or in enclosed spaces.

instructions.heading: Grill without scorching
instructions.action: Place patties on the grill and cook 5 to 6 minutes without pressing. Turn with a wide spatula and cook another 5 to 6 minutes, reducing heat if sugars darken too quickly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Patties release cleanly, hold together, and brown deeply without blackened sugar.
instructions.safetyNote: Switch to a clean spatula after the raw side has been cooked; never press out juices.

instructions.heading: Verify ground-meat temperature
instructions.action: Insert a calibrated thermometer horizontally from the side into the center of multiple patties. Continue cooking, turning as needed, until every checked patty reaches 160°F / 71°C. Boil the clean reserve separately before brushing, if used.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Centers are firm and thermometer-verified; color is not used as the safety test.
instructions.safetyNote: Ground beef and pork require 160°F / 71°C; do not apply the lower whole-cut beef target.

instructions.heading: Rest and serve
instructions.action: Move to a clean platter, rest 3 minutes for juices to settle, and serve hot.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Patties remain moist and intact after resting.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours in a shallow covered container.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill with ventilation. Preheat to medium, oil lightly, and establish separate raw and cooked spatulas, platters, and thermometer access.
targetInternalTemperature: 160°F / 71°C in the center of every representative ground beef-and-pork patty; no lower whole-cut target applies
visualDonenessCues: Patties hold together and are deeply browned without burned sugar
Multiple patties reach 160°F / 71°C when probed horizontally from the side
foodSafetyNotes: Keep ground beef and pork at or below 40°F / 4°C and do not rinse or taste them raw.
Use separate raw and cooked utensils, parchment, and platters.
Reserve any glaze before raw contact and discard all raw-contact seasoning.
Cook ground beef-and-pork patties to 160°F / 71°C; color is not a substitute for a thermometer.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify labels and protect raw and cooked grill zones from allergen and microbial cross-contact.

substitutions: An all-beef version needs separate fat, moisture, and binding tests.
Use verified gluten-free tamari only after checking the full label.
ingredientSourcing: Choose freshly ground beef and pork with intact cold packaging and current use-by dates.
Ask the butcher to package the meats separately and keep them below ready-to-eat foods in transit.
makeAhead: Shape patties up to 12 hours ahead, cover, and refrigerate below ready-to-eat foods; cook within the ground meat's labeled use-by window.
storage: Refrigerate cooked patties in a shallow airtight container within 2 hours and use within 4 days, consistent with general cooked-leftover guidance pending review.
reheating: Reheat once to 165°F / 74°C in a covered skillet or oven, then serve immediately; avoid repeated cooling and reheating.
leftovers: Crumble properly refrigerated reheated patties into a rice bowl only after they reach the reheating target.
servingSuggestions: Serve one or two patties per person with rice and banchan
Brush lightly with boiled clean reserve only after temperature verification

faq.question: Does tteokgalbi contain rice cake?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The name is associated with the pounded, shaped texture; this beef-and-pork formulation contains no rice cake.

faq.question: Why is the target 160°F instead of 145°F?
faq.answer: These are ground beef-and-pork patties, so the official ground-meat minimum is 160°F / 71°C rather than the whole-cut beef target.
